exploration.title: Heat House
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Compare wall and window heat-transfer power, then track how transferred energy accumulates at fixed temperatures.
exploration.question: How do wall insulation, window area and elapsed time change heat-transfer power and energy when temperatures stay fixed?
exploration.explanation: Thermal energy transfers from warmer places toward cooler places. Power is the rate of energy transfer in watts (joules per second); energy transferred over time is reported in joules, megajoules and kilowatt-hours. Insulation adds thermal resistance and slows transfer through the wall path; it does not create thermal energy. Real buildings transfer energy by conduction through materials, convection with moving fluids and radiation by electromagnetic waves. This steady-state model folds assembly effects into fixed U-factors instead of calculating those mechanisms separately. It holds both temperatures steady, treats added windows as replacements for opaque wall inside a 60 m² envelope, and omits the roof, floor, air leaks, sunlight, moisture, thermal bridges, stored heat and equipment. The values are teaching inputs, not measurements, product ratings, a weather forecast or an energy-bill estimate.

experiments.title: Wall insulation
experiments.instruction: Choose Wall insulation. Predict what happens to window heat-transfer power, then Set baseline and Add 10 cm insulation. Keep brick, 8 m² windows, 20°C inside, 0°C outside and 6 h fixed; change only added insulation from 0 to 10 cm.
experiments.observe: Wall power falls from 2066 W to 346 W while window power stays 448 W. Over 6 h, combined transferred energy falls from 15.09 kWh to 4.77 kWh. Explain why changing the wall path leaves the unchanged window path fixed.

experiments.title: Window area
experiments.instruction: Choose Window area. Predict what happens to combined outward power, then Set baseline and Use 18 m² windows. Keep brick, 10 cm insulation, 20°C inside, 0°C outside and 6 h fixed; change only window area from 2 to 18 m² inside the same 60 m² envelope.
experiments.observe: Opaque wall area falls from 58 to 42 m², combined power rises from 498 W to 1288 W, and 6 h energy rises from 2.99 kWh to 7.73 kWh. Explain why both area and U-factor determine this teaching result.

exploration.misconception: Insulation does not generate warmth, and watts are not a temperature or an amount of energy. Insulation slows transfer through its path; at constant power, transferred energy still accumulates with elapsed time.
